source_title: Gyanu must go: CJP backs INDIA bloc's Nov 1 rally seeking Gyanesh Kumar's exit - India Today
source_excerpt:
The CJP has backed the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The campaign raises concerns over electoral roll revisions, voter exclusions and institutional accountability.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has backed the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, accusing the poll body’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise of undermining electoral democracy and raising concerns over the exclusion of eligible voters. Asserting “Gyanu must go”, the party said Kumar had lost the trust required to oversee free and fair elections and called for the Election Commission’s credibility and independence to be restored. In a statement, the CJP said the fundamental principle of democracy was that people chose their government, not the other way around. It argued that the SIR exercise had undermined this principle by raising concerns over the removal of eligible voters from electoral rolls. GYANU MUST GO! The Cockroach Janta Party extends its support to the INDIA Bloc’s November 1 rally. Nation above all! #JaiBhim #JaiHind https://t.co/jbSsRQeHEw— Abhijeet Dipke (@abhijeet_dipke) October 28, 2026 “The fundamental principle of democracy is that people get to choose their government, not that the government gets to choose its voters,” the party said, adding that Kumar’s resignation was necessary to restore public trust in the Election Commission. CJP INVOKES AMBEDKAR’S VISION OF DEMOCRACY The CJP invoked the role of Dr BR Ambedkar in framing the Constitution, arguing that every adult citizen received an equal right to vote regardless of caste, religion, gender, education or economic background. The party said Ambedkar, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and other makers of the Constitution placed their faith in the people at a time when millions of Indians had never participated in an election. “Democracy could only succeed when every citizen had an equal say in deciding the country’s future,” the CJP said, adding that the principle was to bring more citizens into democracy rather than exclude them. RAHUL GANDHI BACKED CJP, DIPKE RESPONDED WITH ‘THANK YOU’ advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The CJP’s support for the INDIA bloc’s rally comes weeks after a rare public exchange between Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke. Rahul had backed a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar after CJP leaders were arrested, saying, “Waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar in a peaceful protest is not a crime. Jailing youth for it is an act of cowardice.” Although Rahul did not name the CJP in his post on X, Dipke responded with a “thank you”. The exchange came after the Congress and the CJP found themselves on the same side of several issues, including exam paper leaks and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, despite largely maintaining their distance in public. ‘PUBLIC IMPEACHMENT’ EVENT SHIFTED TO KHARGE’S HOME The CJP’s endorsement comes as the INDIA bloc prepares for its November 1 rally against Kumar. The opposition alliance has also planned a “public impeachment” event against the CEC on October 30, which it will hold at the official residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge after allegedly facing permission hurdles at other venues. Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said the event would take place at 10, Rajaji Marg, New Delhi, at 3.30 pm. Ramesh accused Kumar of violating the Constitution and undermining electoral democracy. “The CEC has demonstrably violated the letter and spirit of the Constitution. He has systematically subverted the very foundations of our electoral democracy. He has, to put it bluntly, lied to the Supreme Court,” Ramesh said in a post on X. He further accused Kumar of acting on behalf of the ruling leadership, saying, “He has been the willing executioner on behalf of the Diabolical Duo whose turn will come next.” INDIA BLOC RALLY TO FOCUS ON ‘VOTE CHORI’ The October 30 programme was planned as a curtain-raiser for the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan in the national capital. Venugopal said 21 opposition parties had planned to participate in the event against alleged electoral irregularities and the opposition’s “vote chori” charge. The Congress and other opposition parties have been demanding Kumar’s resignation over the SIR exercise and alleged irregularities in the electoral process. The planned rally forms part of their broader campaign seeking accountability from the Election Commission. He added that the programme would involve INDIA bloc parties and participants from across the country. - Ends

कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर 1 नवंबर को नई दिल्ली में होने वाली INDIA गठबंधन की रैली को अपना समर्थन देने की घोषणा की है। 28 अक्टूबर 2026 को सामने आई इस रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, यह राजनीतिक घटनाक्रम चुनाव आयोग के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) अभियान से जुड़े विवादों के बीच आया है।

इंडिया टुडे की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, CJP ने मतदाता सूची संशोधन प्रक्रिया की आलोचना करते हुए कहा कि इससे योग्य मतदाताओं के बाहर होने और लोकतांत्रिक सिद्धांतों के कमजोर होने की आशंका है। पार्टी ने डॉ. बी.आर. अम्बेडकर और जवाहरलाल नेहरू के संवैधानिक दृष्टिकोण का हवाला देते हुए इस बात पर जोर दिया कि सार्वभौमिक वयस्क मताधिकार सभी नागरिकों को मतदान का समान अधिकार प्रदान करता है।

## मुख्य राजनीतिक घटनाक्रम

* **CJP का समर्थन:** CJP नेता अभिजीत देशपांडे (अभिजीत डिपके) ने रामलीला मैदान में 1 नवंबर को होने वाले विरोध प्रदर्शन को समर्थन देने की पुष्टि की और "Gyanu must go" का नारा दिया।
* **सार्वजनिक महाभियोग कार्यक्रम:** INDIA गठबंधन ने अन्य स्थानों पर अनुमति मिलने में कथित बाधाओं के बाद, 30 अक्टूबर को कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खर्गे के आधिकारिक आवास (10, राजाजी मार्ग, नई दिल्ली) पर CEC के खिलाफ "सार्वजनिक महाभियोग" कार्यक्रम आयोजित करने की योजना बनाई थी।
* **विपक्ष के आरोप:** कांग्रेस महासचिव जयराम रमेश सहित विपक्षी नेताओं ने CEC पर संवैधानिक प्रावधानों का उल्लंघन करने और सुप्रीम कोर्ट को गुमराह करने का आरोप लगाया है, जो विपक्ष के "वोट चोरी" अभियान का मुख्य हिस्सा है।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ और सत्यापन

इन घोषणाओं की सत्यता की पुष्टि के लिए नागरिक और observer राजनीतिक दलों के आधिकारिक सोशल मीडिया हैंडल पर जारी बयानों या नई दिल्ली में निर्धारित विरोध कार्यक्रमों को कवर करने वाली मुख्यधारा की मीडिया रिपोर्टों की मदद ले सकते हैं।

en_body:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced its support for the INDIA opposition bloc's planned November 1 rally in New Delhi, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Reported on October 28, 2026, the development follows controversies surrounding the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

According to the source-grounded report by India Today, the CJP criticized the electoral roll revision process, arguing that it risks excluding eligible voters and undermining democratic principles. The party invoked the constitutional vision of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Jawaharlal Nehru, emphasizing that universal adult suffrage guarantees equal voting rights for all citizens.

## Key Developments and Political Context

* **CJP Endorsement:** CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke confirmed support for the upcoming November 1 protest at Ramlila Maidan, using the campaign slogan "Gyanu must go."
* **Public Impeachment Event:** The INDIA bloc planned a pre-event program described as a "public impeachment" of the CEC on October 30 at the official residence of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge located at 10, Rajaji Marg, New Delhi, after facing reported venue permission issues.
* **Broader Allegations:** Opposition leaders, including Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh, have accused the CEC of violating constitutional provisions and misleading the Supreme Court, allegations that form the core of the opposition's "vote chori" (vote theft) campaign.

## Practical Implications and Verification

Citizens and observers looking to verify these announcements can consult official statements released by participating political parties on verified social media channels or refer to mainstream news coverage reporting on the scheduled opposition events in New Delhi.
